{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Contracts — demand-scoped execution edition

**Status:** normative candidate rules for a local experimental publication; not a qualified release or an implemented conformance claim.
**Proposed edition:** `blue-contracts/2026-10-22-demand-scoped-1`.
**Proposed package version:** `1.0.0-demand-scoped.1`; final release metadata is assigned by the canonical build owner.
**Baseline:** [final-gas specification](contracts-final-gas.md).
**Conformance and implementation gates:** [demand-scoped cases](contracts-demand-scoped-conformance.md).

The canonical build assigns the candidate BlueIds from these exact rules and their pinned imports. Prior archived publications and existing specifications remain unchanged. This candidate may be built locally to bind and test the new implementation; it MUST NOT become a production default or a qualified release until the linked conformance gates and normal lifecycle tests pass. Sections 12.1–12.5 define the replacement algorithms and take precedence over the baseline's conflicting whole-certification and whole-closure calls; baseline scheduling and unrelated semantics remain unchanged. The candidate label is not evidence that D1–D5 have passed.

## 1. Contract and compatibility

The new edition defines successful execution as completion of every obligation required by the requested Contracts transition, including its required evidence retention. It does not certify every value transitively reachable from its input, event or result. Blue Language remains the authority for exact identity, effective types, constraints, exact evidence and cyclic proof validation. `strict_certify`/`NativeRuntime.strict` retain their full meaning.

The public cause remains the original exact event and supplied timestamp. Channel Event Checkpoint retains `event: {blueId: ORIGINAL_EVENT_ID}`. Event bytes, signatures and predecessor links MUST NOT be rewritten. This edition introduces neither `entryId` nor `eventProofs`, serialized coverage certificates, external completion tokens or new trusted claims in document content.

All prior editions retain their original processing, certification, gas and storage rules. An exact installed edition binding selects this policy before a request executes; availability, account age, author-supplied labels and cache state cannot select it. New and old account runtimes may coexist in one process without sharing edition-dependent conclusions. Cross-edition processing of one managed document is outside this release.

Unless explicitly revised here, retain the final-gas edition's operation selection, deterministic scheduling, protected markers, occurrence identities, lifecycle, generalization, failure observations and public API. Coordination determines signed source validity, authority, history and admission under its separately selected edition; Contracts does not infer these from an event-shaped value.

## 2. One obligation policy

An invocation has a private working context and an obligation set. An obligation identifies:

```
(edition, input snapshot, original cause, current exact member/view,
 contextual Recipe, processor role, operation/purpose, required coverage)
```

The tuple is a semantic identity, not a required new serialized format. Coverage denotes what was established: exact identity/evidence, effective header, contextual predicate, selected value/subtree, managed occurrence, or complete Language value/definition. These categories MUST NOT be treated as interchangeable trust levels. A contextual predicate fact is not a whole-value certificate, even when its exact BlueId equals a completely certified value in another role.

The native processor and the actual operation determine obligations. Source availability MUST NOT change their meaning. A successful full-content execution and a successful missing-unused-content execution on the same source MUST have identical observations and logical gas. A required missing record produces `NEEDS_RESOURCES`; invalid evidence produces the native validation error; unsupported semantics produces an explicit failure, never a successful filter mismatch or a false absence.

Obligations are extended by actual observations and writes. Conditional BEX evaluation adds obligations for its discriminant and selected branch under normal BEX semantics. An unselected branch does not acquire an execution obligation merely because it is reachable. Metadata and constraints may nevertheless require inspecting it. This rule does not allow the processor to ignore an already established obligation when a resource is unavailable.

There is no exemption set keyed only by BlueId. The same exact body may be opaque predecessor data and a required current operand. The latter role MUST perform its own contextual validation and demand missing content. Repeated obligations may reuse verified facts only when their complete context and coverage agree; metering follows the logical work rule, not physical reuse.

## 3. Native observations and contextual validity

The current Java interfaces provide building blocks, not a ready-made general scoped certificate:

| Operation | Actual interface | Meaning and restriction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact root/evidence | `NativeRuntime.identity`, `NativeRuntime.open`; `RuntimeBridge.open` | Exact record and owning proof are verified when opened. A hash/reference alone does not establish type validity. |
| Effective contextual header | `NativeRuntime.head/readHead(Recipe, runtime)` | Preserve effective type, inherited contributions, requirements and metadata. A header is not a full certificate. |
| Descendant selection | `NativeRuntime.child(Head, key)`; `RuntimeBridge.child/select` | Derive the child from the effective parent Recipe; do not replace it with a standalone reference that loses `valueType`, `itemType` or inherited requirements. |
| Contextual whole subtree | `NativeRuntime.validate(Recipe, runtime, goal)` | Validates that selected subtree using Language semantics. It may demand descendants; it is not a partial-validation flag. |
| Containing constraints | `runtime.validateConstraints(Head, root)` | Run native constraints against the actual effective head. Constraint evaluation may demand more content. This call alone does not check every metadata, type or structural obligation. |
| Native type/definition | `NativeRuntime.ancestry/subtype`, `NativeRuntime.strict(...,"definition")` where whole definition is required | Do not replace native subtype, fixed-value, specification or schema logic with string/type-name checks. |
| Scalar observation | `RuntimeBridge.project` on the selected Recipe | Projection consumes a value; its result must not be hashed as the original exact identity. |
| Full certificate | `NativeRuntime.strict` / `RuntimeBridge.certify` | Unchanged complete Language check; only actual successful full checks may populate its cache. |

Every operation that observes a node MUST establish the validity of the information it uses, including the containing constraints that govern that observation. Own and inherited type/schema, `specification`, fixed values, labels, merge policy and container metadata are not optional simply because the selected descendant is otherwise well typed. Requiredness, presence and absence are resolved through the effective parent; unavailable evidence is not absence.

A processor MAY defer a child's value validation only if neither its action nor a governing predicate requires that value. It MUST still check governing predicates that apply at its selected container boundary. For example, an invalid `maxFields` on `contracts` cannot be bypassed by validating each contract separately. A `valueType` constraint on `count` cannot be discharged by certifying the number outside its parent. A specification reference required for the selected node must resolve and validate with Language's definition semantics.

The lowering of each native handler into these obligations MUST be listed and tested. If a Language predicate requires the entire subtree, invoke that native predicate with the required evidence; do not substitute a structural guess. If the existing interfaces cannot express a necessary selected predicate without imposing unrelated full validation, record an executable reproducer and an explicit API/design decision before publication. This draft does not authorize altering Language or BEX semantics or introducing a global skip-validation switch.

### 3.1 First bounded lowering: required containers

The initial additive Java primitive observes an already-required object or list container. It does not decide optional-child presence and is not a replacement for complete snapshot validation. It verifies authored and effective type/specification/item/key/value metadata through native definition checks. For an empty effective constraint description, there is no constraint predicate to evaluate: after explicit required-container shape checks, this lowering does not call the native constraint routine's incidental concrete-child counting. A nonempty effective constraint continues through native evaluation and may widen the demand, except for the required-object presence lowering below. This is a Contracts obligation/gas-plan decision, not a change to Language strict validation.

A container/header obligation MUST retain its original contextual Recipe and discharge its governing definitions. After constructing the native effective Head and establishing presence using the existing native occurrence/root rules, it MAY discharge the effective constraint without native object-field counting if and only if the Head kind is `object`, the checked occurrence is present, and the effective constraints description contains exactly `required` with a Boolean value. The required-presence predicate is then satisfied; no field-count predicate exists. This MUST still charge the existing `schemaPredicateEvaluated` obligation for `required` and MUST NOT establish a whole-value certificate or reusable value obligation.

Absent occurrences, scalar/list/none kinds, and every other effective constraint combination MUST continue through native validation. Inherited constraints are part of the effective description. In particular, `minFields`, `maxFields`, key/value/item rules and required scalar/list payload checks MUST NOT be bypassed. Governing metadata and observed ordinary records retain their existing obligations. Native presence remains authoritative: an object-shaped definition alone is not a present value. Legacy validation and tariffs are unchanged.

Canonical key validation is currently exposed only through whole native subtree validation. The first primitive therefore widens a container with explicit `keyType` to complete selected validation; it does not claim lazy `keyType` support or duplicate Language's key parser. Actual selected-value use performs full selected exact certification plus the contextual Recipe validation, preserving parent `itemType`/`valueType` requirements. Neither the container observation nor its return value is stored as a full certificate. These restrictions remain explicit until tested lowering is expanded.

### 3.2 Handler requirements

Discovery reads the effective contract map, keys, runtime type ancestry, ordering and fields used to classify/route a declaration. It MUST NOT project or certify an entire workflow merely to identify its handler. The exact installed runtime catalogue supplies the handler policy; business document IDs and workflow IDs do not.

Before an eligible handler executes, validate its consumed declaration fields, filter and selected step under their contextual Recipes. Filters preserve native presence, refinement and constraint semantics; only proven mismatch returns false. A request schema or authorization predicate that requires a payload makes that payload required. The same applies to ordinary observers: operation routing is not an exemption from an observer's actual reads.

Initial supported handler policies MUST be derived from the actual Order, Activation and mandate primitive inventory. Adding a recognized custom runtime without a defined obligation policy MUST fail explicitly, not inherit a permissive policy. This is a runtime capability rule, not a business whitelist.

## 4. Boundary obligations

| Boundary | Mandatory obligations | Deferred content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh input | Source/exact identity; reject forged protected markers; effective managed shape, declaration discovery and initialization requirements | Unselected workflow bodies/branches except where governing constraints require them |
| Snapshot restore | Closed envelope, expected and recomputed commitment, release/bindings, exact member roots and cyclic ownership, root/edge/lifetime/serial/marker integrity, contextual structural constraints | Unused ordinary descendants and historical event operands; no blanket full-body fact |
| Event ingress | Original exact event identity, supplied timestamp, contextual fields needed by dispatch and applicable constraints; signed admission remains host responsibility | Predecessor payload/foreign operand content not required by this action |
| Channel/checkpoint | Native marker type and applicable contextual constraints, channel lifetime, exact event reference, timestamp scalar/range and native channel progression rules | Reachable history not consumed by these checks |
| Handler/BEX | Selected declaration/step, current read operands, native filter and required parameter constraints, captured view/resolver and logical meter | Unselected branch bodies and untouched value descendants |
| Patch | Native construction, selected path and target context, protected-state/generalization rules, constraints affected by the write, reconciled graph/occurrences | Unchanged subtrees only where their governing obligations are unaffected |
| Finalization | All outstanding local/graph obligations, stable identities and cyclic proofs, sealed source state, pending reactions and required retention | No obligation may be silently dropped at this boundary |
| Completion/receive | Local verified origin, before/after views, cause, edition/bindings, complete execution-unit membership, tickets and exact predecessor compatibility | No assumption of whole-value certification from a valid completion |
| Export/cold restore | Exact retained records and owning proofs sufficient to reconstruct the specified restore/receive obligations; expected commitments | Optional unused closure must not leak through inline ancestors |

A patch changing a type, schema, specification, container structure or managed declaration invalidates dependent obligations. Re-evaluate them on the new contextual view before the next step observes it. Do not reuse the unchanged child BlueId's old contextual result when its parent requirements changed. The existing native generalization and constraint rules remain authoritative; preservation of their effects must be demonstrated rather than replaced by post-hoc acceptance.

Identity-only observation must remain identity-only even for an inline body. Real scalar/subtree access must perform the same contextual work for inline and referenced forms. Reading a checkpoint timestamp through native projection is legitimate; rewriting its persisted representation or relaxing integer checks is not.

## 5. Invocation and publication algorithm

The following pseudocode specifies ordering and invariants. `require_for` is a proposed internal obligation operation, not an existing Language API. Its handler-specific lowering and the complete executable reference implementation are release gates.

```
execute(edition, input, originalEvent, time):
    assert installed exact edition/bindings
    tx := fork input state, Language evidence context, obligation facts,
               archive updates, completion registrations and retained output
    require_for(tx, RESTORE_OR_INPUT, input)
    require_for(tx, EVENT_DISPATCH, originalEvent, time)
    run existing deterministic Contracts scheduling in tx
        before each observation: require_for(tx, selected contextual role)
        before installing each patch: native construct/generalize and
            require_for(tx, affected contextual write obligations)
        after patch: reconcile and finalize required local/graph obligations
    require_for(tx, FINALIZE, resulting managed graph)
    retained := prepare_required_records(tx, input, result, originalEvent)
    verify retained records can satisfy cold restore and local receive obligations
    seal outcome and its cause/edition/member bindings
    atomically install tx context, stable state, retained output, archive and
        process-local completion establishment
    return APPLIED
on missing, invalid, exhausted or incomplete execution/required retention:
    discard tx effects, evidence additions, selected facts and registrations
    return the edition's failure/incomplete result against original input
```

Preparing retention is part of success, not an optional operation after completion establishment. A late export failure cannot leave a newly capturable result, advanced checkpoint, archive entry or reusable selected fact behind. Preserve previous prepared/committed output. Repeating the exact input/event/time after obtaining the required evidence runs against the original stable input and does not duplicate a previously partial mutation.

This local atomic boundary is distinct from durable host publication. The host's existing journal transaction MUST atomically publish the completed state/evidence, original cause, progress, emitted effects and retry obligations. A transient local result is not evidence of durable commit. Host failure cannot publish a receipt/progress record without its required content. This draft does not require a new journal or service.

## 6. Completion guarantee and normal receiving

A new-edition completion establishes: this installed edition executed the identified input and original cause through all required obligations, obtained the exact resulting managed state and ordered output, and prepared all evidence required by this completion's storage/receive contract. It does NOT assert complete Language validity of every transitively reachable value.

Preserve the existing local capability boundary:

1. Only the actual successful local attempt may establish an outcome; bind input snapshot identity, event BlueId/timestamp, release, exact runtime bindings, before/after member views, receipt, units and ordered effects.
2. `capture` requires that established local outcome and matching process-local provenance. Validate selected members, owner birth rules and complete unit inclusion. A user-provided receipt, after-body or matching hash is insufficient.
3. `receive`/live receive verifies issuer, capability lifetime, cause, compatible exact edition/bindings, owned members, captured occurrence tickets and predecessor views. It validates its own contextual obligations. Incorporation is not full certification of the source's opaque closure.
4. Process restart does not deserialize a trusted capability from input bytes. The installed privileged local `CompletionReader` may recover an atomically committed local completion, verify descriptor/receipt and bindings, restore required before/after evidence under this edition, and re-establish local provenance. Arbitrary imported snapshots cannot invoke this path.
5. Modified, foreign, expired, overlapping or incompatible completion records remain rejected. This edition does not define public third-party execution proofs.

The existing descriptor's `release`, `runtimes`, before/after vectors, event, timestamp and receipt carry these bindings; there is no new user-authored coverage flag. Changing an edition changes its immutable specification identity and therefore its interpretation. The reference implementation MUST explicitly apply the new guarantee at establishment and rehydration; deleting `UNESTABLISHED_SOURCE_COMPLETION` is not an implementation.

## 7. Retention, privacy and cyclic exact content

Compute required records from the obligation roles and replay/restore requirements, not from whatever extra content happens to be cached. A record may be required in one role even if another role defers the same BlueId. Retaining unused private bodies because they were available in the full-control runtime violates deterministic scoped export/privacy.

For acyclic exact records, preserve exact identity while emitting finite child references; verify identity after serialization. Traversal follows the required roles. Do not serialize an inline ancestor wholesale when it contains an excluded descendant. A missing excluded descendant is not replaced by null, empty content or a fabricated value.

For a cyclic member, retain and verify the Language owning-set proof and required member body using the existing canonical proof/body mechanism. Do not emit an ordinary acyclic `mode: exact` record under `master#i`. Deduplicate with a finite identity/context/role work set, not by dropping owning proofs or globally whitelisting an identity. Historical graph edges such as A(T) → B(T) → A(T−1) remain exact historical edges, not latest-state aliases.

Cold restore opens and verifies actual supplied exact records and owning proofs, then derives the required obligations anew under the selected edition. Serialized statements of prior validation are not trusted. Missing content needed for these obligations must still wait/fail. ### 12.5 Logical obligation traversal and reuse

This edition introduces a separate obligation ledger; it does not change the old edition's `LogicalWork.validate/visit` algorithm or select behavior by broadening `finalGas()`. One attempt owns the ledger and meter. A chunk continuation copies both; an independent attempt or cold processor starts a new ledger. Failed fork work cannot publish facts or completion, even when its returned diagnostic reports gas already consumed.

The ledger key is `(contextual Recipe.key, obligation kind, coverage)`. Kinds are `container`, `definition`, and `value`; coverage identifies the complete selected contextual subtree for `value`, and the observed container/predicate/header set for `container`. Ancestor observations have their own keys. An unchanged BlueId under a different Recipe or coverage is a distinct obligation. Container/definition success never establishes a value key. Global Language/bridge caches do not affect this logical ledger.

The reference algorithm is:

```text
require(obligation):
    first require each enclosing container in outermost-to-innermost order
    if this exact obligation key succeeded in this invocation:
        charge validationProofReused once
        return its previously established obligation result
    dispatch by kind using the algorithms below
    record success only after the native check succeeds
```

For `container`, open each authored Recipe part through `LogicalWork.open` (which charges `nodeManifestOpened` once per exact ID per invocation), construct the unchanged native effective Head, and follow its applicable governing definitions with `definition` obligations. Each type edge followed charges `typeEdgeFollowed`; each explicitly selected ordinary child edge charges `objectMemberRead`, or `listItemRead` for an index. Charge `schemaPredicateEvaluated` once for each key of the effective constraints' `describe()` map, in sorted-key order. Perform the native required-container check and native effective predicate evaluation, subject only to the required-object presence lowering in §3.1: an effective object occurrence established present by native rules, with exactly the Boolean `required` constraint, discharges that predicate without incidental field counting while retaining its predicate charge. Empty effective constraints have zero predicate charges and no concrete-count walk. Incidental resolver/cache work inside the native predicate implementation is physical work, not a second logical traversal or a whole-subtree value charge. Predicate-driven widening invokes an explicit `value` obligation, whose own charges are separate; it cannot silently establish a value certificate from the container result.

For `definition`, traverse the exact definition evidence needed by native definition certification in deterministic native field/list order. Each distinct exact manifest opened is charged through the same invocation `LogicalWork.open`. Traversed ordinary fields charge `objectMemberRead`; items charge `listItemRead`; type edges charge `typeEdgeFollowed`. Deduplicate exact cycles within this definition traversal; do not regard a cycle visit as successful native certification. Then certify with goal `definition`. Do not evaluate a definition's declared minimum, maximum, enumeration or required-value constraints against the definition as if it were a value. Owning proofs use the native evidence verifier. Only successful native definition certification establishes this definition obligation.

For `value`, use an edition-specific traversal retaining the existing `LogicalWork.visit` scalar/list/object predicate accounting on the selected contextual Recipe, including its comparisons, text blocks, integer limbs, member examinations and pending value-proof keys. The old `carriedRoots` early return is disabled: a captured/portable source identity alone is not successful contextual value coverage. The old `previous` equality shortcut is likewise disabled unless the corresponding same-invocation contextual value obligation already succeeded. Do not call the old unmodified `visit` as the new reference algorithm. Its traversal is rooted at the selected Recipe, not the surrounding document. Then require both native strict selected evidence and `NativeRuntime.validate(selectedRecipe, context, "value")`. Publish the logical pending proof keys only after both checks succeed. A prior container or definition obligation does not enter that value-proof set. Do not pass an enclosing whole-root `previous` value to skip a changed contextual requirement; unchanged-subtree reuse requires the same contextual Recipe key and previously successful value coverage in this invocation.

In the new edition, establishing the identity of an explicit `Exact.Ref` reuses that reference's exact identifier. This identity-only case returns `local=false` and MUST NOT open the referenced body, rebuild it or charge identity hashing for that body, including when the reference appears as a part of local identity construction. It MUST NOT establish an `established` fact, a value certificate or successful contextual value coverage. Constructed local values retain their existing native identity construction and hash charges. A later required value read or owning-proof verification still establishes its own native obligations; an explicit reference is not evidence of its target's validity. This clarification does not alter legacy edition tariffs.

Handler ordering, BEX execution, patch construction/generalization, graph construction, emitted-event accounting and semantic exact identity construction retain their existing tariff operations. Replace only calls whose old purpose was whole-root validation with the declared obligation algorithm. Record preparation/serialization and fresh transport verification do not add independent semantic gas; exact identity construction already charged by the semantic operation is not charged again because an exporter chooses a different equivalent record encoding. A failed required read, predicate, record preparation or capability prerequisite leaves the input snapshot, prior prepared package, archive and completion registry unpublished. Snapshot wire identity and original event references are never rewritten to encode obligation state.

Qualification MUST compare full/missing and warm/cold logical results for these rules, including a single exact ID read in two different contextual Recipes, container-then-value aliasing, chunk continuation and failed-attempt retry. These are new-edition tariffs; old edition golden gas and receipts remain unchanged.

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Receiver-relative admission and per-node replay — edition draft

Status: frozen normative candidate for the next local, unqualified publication.
This is a distinct rules source; the frozen v3 publication remains unchanged.
Not a published edition, implementation claim, or modification of any frozen
Coordination rules. Publication requires synchronized Contracts completion rules,
reference algorithms, new package identities and passing conformance evidence.
Old editions retain their original Q06/Q13 and publication behavior.

The full provider protocol in the included `coordination.md` remains normative
except where this document explicitly replaces a rule. That baseline has SHA-256
`194550d8dc90bb5a591d8e9cb05ec7c7c16e328ffe29c5517948538aac8a84b6`.
In particular, retain its wire schemas, signatures, authenticated range chains,
access grants, operations and provider content authorization. Its global
operation-target history prerequisite is replaced by section 2 below, and its
Contracts execution dependency is the exact demand-scoped edition selected by
this publication. Provider entry admission validates every required envelope,
type/contextual constraint, signature, chain and binding obligation without
assuming full certification of opaque payload references; payload constraints
that actually require content still demand that content. This is a new-edition
boundary policy, not a change to Language `strict_certify`.

## Retained transport boundary

This edition consumes the existing provider transport without replacing its signed
objects. The explicit data-only `RetainedTransport` dependency is package
`BS8vv7BS6hd3ecLyouphhMoPokPAjzzwVLPd83WjHL3x`, archive SHA-256
`b96ec4011bb0512d896a58e37d3c63ca3531c06244b2d0777cfdd5a106198b88`.
It supplies exact definition and specification witnesses, not an execution
protocol requirement or permission to install the previous execution handlers.

The executable Timeline Access and Timeline Access Update accept retained Signed
Timeline identities in `allowedTimelines`. The new Public Timeline Channel binds
the retained Timeline Provider; the new Timeline Channel binds retained Signed
Timeline and Actor values. The new Timeline Access Response carries retained
Provider Attestation values in `publication` and `lastEntry`. Their existing
signature, chain, actor, grant and reachability checks remain mandatory. Raw key
and signature values retain their existing constraints. The Get Timeline Access
request and access document remain members of this new edition.

Provider transport entries, timeline identities, actor identities, checkpoints,
range evidence and signatures are not rewritten or re-signed for this edition.
This boundary does not equate distinct exported type identities or declare fresh
transport exports to be subtypes of retained definitions. Producers of the
supported retained transport continue to use its original exact types. Other
exports retain their explicit authored schemas; their presence is not a claim
that an arbitrary mixed-edition envelope satisfies those schemas.

## 1. Inputs and evidence boundaries

An input has its original signed Timeline entry and full canonical order
`K = (timestamp, timelineId, entryId)`. Contracts receives the original
`event: {blueId: entryId}` and original time; neither a replacement entry nor a
proof sidecar is introduced. Authenticating the entry, establishing a verified
source prefix, authorizing its actor, and executing it are separate obligations.
Knowing an entry identity is not evidence that its payload or authority is valid.

A receiver is a logical document lineage with a specific member/channel lifetime.
A receiving occurrence additionally identifies its source, path and generation.
Source processing history and an occurrence's history of receiving source work
are distinct. Sharing an acquisition does not merge these obligations.

`PRE(R,K)` is the exact receiver view established from work strictly before K,
including earlier attachment prerequisites and terminal input dispositions.
It includes the genuine original document identity, the ordered established
versions of that lineage before K, and the applicable declarations and authority.
It does not include a later version merely because its content is locally cached.
Completeness requires the existing verified source-prefix conditions, pending
work checks and exact predecessor proofs. A timestamp alone is not a boundary.

Missing evidence needed to establish PRE is a wait. A recursive visit is not a
proof of completeness. An uploaded initialized body is not a substitute for its
required history. Contextual constraints and actual reads remain obligations of
the selected Contracts edition; opaque references do not discharge them.

## 2. Q06: request selection relative to the receiver

The following classifier concerns operation dispatch, not ordinary event
observation. First establish the entry's framing, signature, source membership,
canonical order and complete PRE(R,K). If these prerequisites are missing, wait;
if they are invalid, retain the existing specific rejection. Do not fetch the
request's target body simply to classify an exact-version mismatch.

Let `current` be the exact document identity in PRE and `ownPast` the genuine
original identity plus every established own-lineage version strictly before K.
These are identities established by the receiver's history, not all identities
known to a global store. The original identity remains usable for non-exact
requests after initialization and subsequent changes.

```
classifyOperation(request, R, K):
    pre = requireCompletePRE(R, K)
    if request has no document target:
        return SELECT_USING_CURRENT_DECLARATIONS
    t = request.document
    if request.requireExactDocumentVersion:
        if t == pre.current: return ELIGIBLE
        if t in pre.ownPast: return REJECT_STALE_EXACT
        return OUTSIDE_EXACT_PRE_VIEW
    if t == pre.current or t in pre.ownPast:
        return ELIGIBLE
    if authenticated established lineage evidence proves t belongs elsewhere:
        return OUTSIDE_LINEAGE
    return WAIT_TARGET_HISTORY
```

`OUTSIDE_EXACT_PRE_VIEW` is an operation no-match for this receiver at K. It
makes no claim that t is globally foreign, invalid, or unavailable. In particular,
a future own version mismatches at K whether or not it is cached. This is an
explicit new-edition rule. It is not the old rule with a missing-content error
caught and converted to no-match. An incomplete own prefix cannot use this rule.

`ELIGIBLE` is not authorization or success. Resolve the actual operation/channel,
its schema, actor/mandate and business prerequisites in PRE. Missing required
operands wait; established denial rejects. A non-exact request to an unknown
identity still waits unless actual evidence establishes a different lineage.
Neither inequality nor inability to fetch proves that distinction.

Independently select ordinary observer channels from the same original entry.
An operation outside the receiver's audience does not suppress an otherwise
eligible observer. Such an observer may legitimately need payload data and wait
for it. Operation-path rejection/no-match is scoped separately from any real
observer processing; a feeder must not stamp a whole-entry rejection that hides
an eligible observer. All applicable paths must settle before this input is
complete for the receiver. If observation executes, only its actual Contracts
result may establish a checkpoint. A pure operation rejection/no-match establishes
only a private InputDisposition, never a fictitious Contracts checkpoint.

A disposition binds original entry and K, receiver lineage/lifetime, member and
channel generations, exact PRE and verified source/authority evidence. A settled
path cannot be resurrected by later state in that lifetime. Other receivers and
new generations remain independently evaluated. Publish decisions atomically
with any actual receiver result; do not advance past unresolved selected work.

## 3. Q13: raw node establishment and replay

Every lineage starts from its genuine pre-initialization content. Record that
exact reference before initialization. An already initialized reference follows
the existing-history attachment algorithm below; it is never treated as raw.

For a genuinely new raw child captured by a parent attempt at Kbirth:

1. Retain Contracts' raw source and actual creation provenance. Establish the
   child's own initialization semantics as for standalone admission of that raw
   source. Do not inject a fabricated event/time into initialization. Creation
   provenance remains host/runtime evidence and is not substituted for raw input.
2. Discover the child's required sources using the new edition's ordinary
   source/authority rules. Its replay frontier starts at its own initialization,
   not the parent's last processed order, inherited channel cursor or birth time.
3. Establish its ordered history from the beginning through Kbirth **inclusive**.
   Execute each selected original entry once for its own lineage/channel lifetime.
   Lack of relevant access, authority or content remains a real prerequisite.
4. Deliver retained child results through the completion receiving kernel to the
   eligible occurrence. This turn has no external parent seed. It must not invoke
   the parent's creating operation again or replay the parent's direct history.
5. Record source processing and occurrence receiving separately. Persist pending
   prerequisites and source/receiving positions so a restart resumes the same
   obligations. Do not expose the creating graph as stable while required child
   catch-up or receiving work remains unfinished.

The creating attempt still has its normal rollback boundary: a failed attempt
cannot expose a successful child. Separately committed source work can survive a
later receiving failure; it is reused through verified completion provenance,
not executed again. Intermediate positions retain their non-stable status.
Publication of a stable result must include all required owner/member results,
origin mappings and completed receiving obligations atomically.

Equal timestamps use the full K ordering: earlier ties precede the birth, the
birth entry is eligible exactly once for the child, and later ties remain later
work. The parent is not reseeded at any tie. If a child declaration appears while
processing Kbirth, the dispatcher must not also deliver that same entry as an
additional external live seed after replay has covered it.

### Historical channel activation: scan, causal and attachment coordinates

A newly installed channel lifetime is an ACTIVATION continuation, distinct from
raw-node INITIAL replay. Retain its member/channel/generation, exact committed
activation snapshot and receipt, scanActivationBound A, causalVisibilityBound V,
and original examined full-K cursor. A is the installing invocation's original
input K; V is the maximum full-K bound of the installing invocation itself and all its
causal ancestors.
Outer child attachment visibility Kbirth remains a separate coordinate.

ACTIVATION examines authenticated source entries strictly before A. Raw INITIAL
replay examines its own sources inclusively through Kbirth. Neither boundary is
changed by cached future content or wall-clock time. Installing an existing
channel does not silently consume the installing entry a second time.

For an activation delivery of original K, PRE_ACTIVATION is the exact invocation
prestate established by a contiguous shared receiver causal publication chain
anchored at the activation receipt. Include all earlier scheduled applicable
lifetime turns and receiving results, not merely this lifetime's own turns.
Select operation declarations, receiver actor-policy/business state and exact
current/own-past target classification from that proved prestate. The original
lineage identity remains available for nonexact targeting. Original-K source,
signature, mandate, grant and revocation history remains the authority bound;
a later grant at A never retroactively authorizes the original K.

For a supported canonical Mandates/Mandate Authority, signed-prefix admission and authority-header reads require the contextual authority header, its actor, its closed field set, and an authored original-mandate identity. Only an exact reference occurrence governed solely by the canonical Mandate Authority.mandate declaration may defer that declaration's Mandate value/type obligation until owned original-mandate history before the entry's order key is available. Additional contextual contributions, requirements, type narrowing, or inline governing metadata retain ordinary required-value validation. After resolving that history and before granting authority, the original contextual mandate occurrence MUST satisfy its full value/type obligations. Header admission, retention, and reuse establish neither a whole-value certificate nor authorization; signature, actor, history, approval, status, participant, and scope checks remain mandatory.

A deterministic worklist completes activation prerequisites before the next
ordinary receiver input. Select the minimum original full K within ready
obligations, retaining per-lifetime cursors and exact predecessor receipts.
Equal-K deliveries may share an invocation only if their actual receiver
prestate is proved identical; otherwise execute in ascending `(member identifier, channel name, generation)`
order: the first two use the existing canonical string ordering, followed by the
numeric generation. Map iteration order is not a scheduling rule.
Nested activation retains its own strictly-before scan bound and inherits causal
visibility. For example, L3 installed at original K10 during A100 replay scans
before K10 but remains visible at100, never at10. An earlier logical input cannot
observe effects from a future causal ancestor merely because they were cached.

Operation dispositions bind these coordinates and their exact receiver prestate.
Terminal-only progress, retired/replaced lifetimes and actual receipts remain
separate. A repeated worklist key is unresolved until every local/source/receiving
premise is proved. No global original-K monotonicity shortcut, latest-head
substitution, checkpoint rewrite or parent reseeding establishes completeness.

Conformance additionally covers shared L1/L2 state, nested decreasing scan bounds,
exact-current/stale and nonexact-original targeting, original-time grant/revoke,
full-K ties and persisted restart between installation and historical delivery.

### Existing source and occurrence attachment

An established source retains its original birth, identity and source history.
Attaching it at K freezes the last established source position from work strictly
before K, including that source's earlier attachment prerequisites. Reject a
supplied initialized position beyond this goal. Apply contiguous missing source
successors through the goal without repeating initialization or source effects.
A K-live step then uses its own exact checkpoint/disposition and is not duplicated.

Receiving old source work is effective at the receiving attachment boundary for
receiver history queries, while Contracts keeps the source's original cause/time.
Do not rewind parent checkpoints. Finish required attachment work before the
parent's next input. Detach retires an occurrence, not source history; reattach
creates a new generation and cannot inherit retired pending receiving tickets.

Member origin keys remain exact across promotion/re-root/cold restore. Runtime
constructor keys and independent standalone root keys must not be silently
merged. State-equality conformance compares the child document projections;
completion reuse additionally requires compatible member origins and before-view.
Exact state parity requires the same raw source, applicable semantic context and
relevant authenticated histories. Different parent-imposed constraints are not
assumed equivalent. The same raw source in an independent account is independently
established, not a portable capability to adopt another account's local completion.

## 4. Temporal dependency algorithm and cycles

A pending history obligation is keyed by logical lineage, exact bound, phase
(initialization, before-view, source execution or receiving), and occurrence
generation when applicable. Dependencies retain their bounds; do not collapse
`A before K1` and `A before K2` into one visited document flag.

Maintain unresolved obligations and exact dependency edges. A completed memo can
be reused only for the same obligation and verified evidence. On a repeated
unresolved key, record the edge and analyze the component; never return complete
just because a DFS has encountered it before.

- A historical edge that reduces the bound is ordinary predecessor work. Resolve
  its finite established prefix, then its dependents. Example: A before K30 needs
  B before K20, whose earlier attachment needs A before K10. A's established
  initialization/K5 prefix terminates this chain; this is not a live cycle.
- A missing predecessor, content record or verified prefix is a resource/history
  wait. Repetition does not turn it into an error or authorize a guessed state.
- A live cyclic component may use the existing Contracts component algorithm
  only after every member's exact compatible pre-view and external prerequisites
  are established. Select the canonical representative and publish the complete
  atomic owner set. This resolves simultaneous live computation, not absent past.
- A same-bound proof cycle with no established pre-view is not evidence that any member exists or is ready. Retain the concrete resource/history wait until genuine prerequisites establish every required pre-view. Reject malformed lifecycle records through their applicable native validation rules. This edition specifies no closed-contradiction witness for impossible-before-initialization cycles; do not infer one from an unresolved SCC, missing predecessor or repeated worklist key. Never manufacture a member or return success because a dependency was visited before.

No arbitrary new iteration ceiling is part of this rule. Native deterministic
work/gas limits still apply to actual execution. The implementation must retain a
bounded diagnostic for an unresolved dependency component without calling it a
success. Ordinary graph recursion alone does not prove inconsistent history.

### 4.1 Reference procedure for established local history

The following procedure consumes authenticated local journal history, not
caller-authored proof claims. It does not replace raw establishment in section 3.

```
proveBefore(receiver, K, journalView):
    queue := [(receiver, K, BEFORE, rootOccurrence)]
    checked := empty map
    while queue is not empty:
        obligation := removeFirst(queue)
        select exact last history position with effectiveOrder < obligation.bound
        require its binding, contiguous predecessors and committed completion link
        read member/edge generations from that position's immutable completion.after
        require the exact expected source version for an incoming occurrence
        require local prefix and earlier timer/attachment/rebase work to be settled
        derive source channels from this selected member, not current-head channels
        if any requirement is unavailable: return its bounded unresolved obligation
        if this exact obligation was checked with the same evidence: continue
        record its checked local premises
        enqueue every selected edge's source-view obligation, retaining generation
    return a token bound to receiver, K and this immutable journal view
```

The checks on an incoming edge also occur on repeated keys. Repetition cannot
hide incompatible expected source positions. A token can select only the entry
whose full K and journal view match it. Future cached versions are not own-past
facts. A source completion that the receiver has not applied cannot satisfy an
edge merely because both document rows exist. Terminal input decisions are
retained prefix evidence, not successful source transitions.

Receiving prerequisites retain the source's original cause bound separately from
the receiving effective boundary. For example, receiving source event100 at
attachment300 may require a source prefix through100 (completeBefore101); it
cannot demand301 solely because the receive is published at300. Conversely, that
completed receive does not prove the receiver's later PRE301: later relevant
source work still needs its own prefix and receiving evidence. These are distinct
obligations in the same time-indexed procedure, not one document-wide visited bit.

## 5. Completion, persistence and resource origin

Use the new Contracts edition's normal completion/receiving API. A result binds
before/after state, original cause, executing edition/runtimes, member origins,
operation scope and the actual validated obligations. A data-only snapshot or
source-prefix witness is not a completion. Local durable recovery may rehydrate
only authenticated journal provenance for that edition and exact result.

Receiving installs the eligible source states before callbacks, preserving
whole-batch order, owner boundaries, generation checks and gas accounting. It
never substitutes direct snapshot patches or an extra parent external seed.
Cold recovery must reconstruct pending admission, source execution and receiving
without granting full Language certification to an operation-scoped result.

A required content identity does not identify a provider. Original cause timeline
alone does not authorize fetching every reference encountered while processing
that cause, especially a reference reached through older history. Provider
selection must use existing authenticated/adopted source provenance and access
mechanisms. Invocation-local required-read provenance also covers native matcher
opens: it relates reported missing identities only through ordinary authored edges
of bodies actually opened by that evaluation. A wrapper-specific read path is not
the only source of such observations. This collector supplies an observed path,
not authenticated provider authority; it does not search imported/provider
inventory or infer authored paths from inherited type fields. This draft does not introduce a wire proof sidecar or unrestricted
search over imported timelines. The exact host mapping for historical obligations
is an implementation gate to resolve with source-access owners before publishing.

## 6. Required executable conformance cases

Each test runs old and new selections where behavior changes; do not update old
expected outcomes. Missing/cached variants use identical admitted logical input.

| Case | Minimal fixture and required outcome in the new edition |
| --- | --- |
| Exact current | Complete PRE at K, target current: dispatch plus normal authority checks. |
| Exact stale | Known own predecessor, exact=true: durable operation rejection, no operation checkpoint/effect. |
| Exact future absent | A future target identity signed into K, future body unavailable: exact mismatch, no fetch. |
| Exact future cached | Same K/PRE/entry as preceding case, later body/history cached: identical decision. |
| Exact other receiver | Private Agreement exact target then child-target operation: child reaches later input without parent fetch. |
| Incomplete PRE | Repeat exact mismatch with required earlier prefix absent: WAIT, then settle after that prefix arrives. |
| Non-exact original | Agent request targets original raw Order after initialization: normal authorized dispatch. |
| Non-exact unknown | Unknown target with no lineage proof: WAIT; no false foreign/no-match. |
| Mixed audience | Exact operation mismatch plus matching ordinary observer: observer receives original event, including real operand WAIT. |
| Raw birth | Counter observer sees K100, birth K200: standalone and embedded raw child have identical complete state/BlueId; parent birth executes once. |
| Ties | Three entries at one timestamp ordered before/equal/after birth: each eligible child effect once, no parent reseed. |
| Existing attach | Attach an established earlier position; contiguous receive only; initialized future position rejected. |
| Reattach | Detach/recreate same path: new generation, source effects unchanged, no transfer of old pending ticket. |
| Decreasing history | A@30 -> B@20 -> A@10 with established K5 prefix: resolves, including after cold reopen. |
| Live SCC | Two established mutually embedded members: coherent component result and atomic publication, no recursion shortcut. |
| Missing cycle predecessor | Same-bound dependency component with one missing external predecessor: durable wait and automatic resume after exact evidence. |
| Malformed initialization receipt | An INITIALIZE Processing Receipt carrying an event, sourceReceipts or attachment is rejected as `INVALID_RECEIPT_KIND` by normal receipt validation. No local completion, initialized member or stable result is established from that claimed receipt. |
| Unestablished dependency component | A repeated same-bound dependency component without every required established pre-view remains WAIT. Missing lifecycle history or a predecessor is not proof of contradiction. Supplying genuine missing evidence resumes the same obligations; if complete compatible pre-views become established, use normal source processing or the existing live-component algorithm. No invented initialization, stable member or recursion-success shortcut. |
| Full acceptance | Real original raw Order, separate Seller/Partner/Customer stores, Seller Agent exact-original mandate, second operation and cold reopen: full state/BlueId equality and no private Agreement acquisition. |

## 7. Publication gates and source anchors

This draft selects exact mismatch-at-PRE semantics rather than claiming universal foreign-target detection. Implementation must expose path-scoped operation and observer outcomes or prove its existing admission representation can express section 2 without suppressing observers. Malformed lifecycle evidence is rejected by its applicable native validation rule; an INITIALIZE Processing Receipt with an event, sourceReceipts or attachment is `INVALID_RECEIPT_KIND`. Missing lifecycle evidence, missing prefixes and unresolved dependency components remain WAIT, including when a worklist encounters the same unresolved key repeatedly. This edition does not define a separate `INVALID_CAUSAL_HISTORY` result for impossible creation cycles: no accepted closed-contradiction witness is specified. Neither absence nor repetition establishes a contradiction, a completion or readiness.

Required design checks before reference implementation: bounded child-only
catch-up/receiving without parent reseeding; initialized child equality without
forged origin adoption; historical demand-to-authorized-source mapping; and the
Contracts completion contract for operation-scoped outputs. None is proven by
this prose. They must be settled in code-backed fixtures before publication.

Baseline anchors (retained, not edited): canonical `coordination.md`, source
coverage/admission around lines 865–925; Core `runtime/final-gas-bridge/spec/
prior-rules.md` Q06 and Q13–Q20. Current reference implementation anchors:
`CoordinationAdmission.verifyAdmission` (global target-known gate and separate observer
selection), `CoordinationHistory.belongs/before/completeBefore` (global version
membership, historical views and recursion), `CoordinationEngine` attachment,
receiving and member publication; `ContractGraph.freshKey` for member origins.
Existing small starting repros are `MinimalRawBirthBoundaryTest` and
`MinimalTemporalHistoryViewTest`; a cached future view test is not by itself an
admission conformance test.
